- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/03/10 (Fri) 19:46
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] According to Christian doctrine, the Holy Spirit is the third person of the Trinity, co-equal and co-eternal with the Father and the Son.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father and, according to some Christian traditions, also from the Son.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In the New Testament, the Holy Spirit is depicted as being active in the world from the beginning of creation and as playing a key role in the work of salvation.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Holy Spirit is present at Jesus' baptism (Mark 1:9-11), comes upon the disciples at Pentecost (Acts 2:1-4), and guides and empowers believers in their Christian walk (Romans 8:14-17).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In the doctrine of the Trinity, the three persons of the Godhead (Father, Son, and Holy Spirit) are distinct but not separate.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Each person is fully God, and yet there is only one God.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Holy Spirit, as the third person of the Trinity, is intimately involved in the divine life and work of God, working in perfect unity with the Father and the Son to accomplish the divine plan of salvation for humanity.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The belief that the Holy Spirit proceeds from both the Father and the Son is known as the "filioque" clause.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The filioque clause was adopted by the Western Church (Roman Catholic Church) in the 6th century and later by some Protestant denominations.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Eastern Orthodox Church rejected the filioque clause, maintaining that the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father alone.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Eastern Orthodox theologians argue that the filioque clause is an erroneous addition to the Nicene Creed that undermines the doctrine of the Trinity.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Eastern Orthodox Church holds that the Father is the sole source of the Holy Spirit, while the Son is begotten of the Father.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] There have been efforts to reconcile the theological differences between the Eastern and Western Churches over the filioque clause, but the issue remains contentious.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] John 4:24 reads, "God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth."
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Christian doctrine of the Trinity teaches that there is one God in three persons - the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
